newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Paraguay Central Bank takes control of Banco Union.
newsitem.headline: Paraguay Central Bank takes control of Banco Union.

text.p: Paraguay's Central Bank announced Monday that it took control of Banco Union, the country's largest private nationally-owned bank, due to liquidity problems.
Central bank spokesman Andres Benitez told Reuters Paraguayan President Juan Carlos Wasmosy will give details of the decision later today in a televised speech. Banco Union was closed Monday.
Union board member Herman Velilla, in remarks to journalists, questioned the decision, although he admitted the bank was going through "liquidity problems."
With some $190 million in deposits, the bank is Parauay's third largest holder of public deposits, and the biggest in private corporate deposits.
Last week authorities took control of Ahorros Paraguayos, a savings and loan institution linked to Banco Union through some of its board members, also due to a lack of liquidity.

Paraguay has been in the grips of a financial crisis since May 1995 which according to official data has required the injection of $500 million in funds. ((-- Jose Maria Amarilla, Asuncion newsroom, 595 21 444527))
